frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of a CONSTITUTED, RAISED-UP ENTITY that issues from and stands upon a foundational source — a "built-up product" together with its constitutive dependence on that source. Concretely: (a) with the building family, a structure erected upon a base (bunyān/binā'/ṣarḥ/bayt/samā' raised min al-qawā'id or 'alā a footing); (b) with the kinship family, a child/descendant as the generatively "built-up" issue and standing extension of a progenitor (ibn/banū/banāt/abnā'). The invariant residue is: derived-standing-entity + its source-relation (source → constituted continuation).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of a CONSTITUTED, RAISED-UP ENTITY that issues from and stands upon a foundational source — a "built-up product" together with its constitutive dependence on that source. Concretely: (a) with the building family, a structure erected upon a base (bunyān/binā'/ṣarḥ/bayt/samā' raised min al-qawā'id or 'alā a footing); (b) with the kinship family, a child/descendant as the generatively "built-up" issue and standing extension of a progenitor (ibn/banū/banāt/abnā'). The invariant residue is: derived-standing-entity + its source-relation (source → constituted continuation).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Two surface sense-families appear, and the invariant sits underneath both. (1) BUILDING. The 11 verbal occurrences all denote erecting a standing structure: "ibnū 'alayhim bunyānā" (18:21) build a structure over them; "ibni lī ṣarḥan" (40:36) build me a tower; "ibni lī 'indaka baytan" (66:11) build me a house; "wa-l-samā'a banaynāhā bi-aydin" (51:47), "banaynā fawqakum sab'an shidādan" (78:12), "am al-samā'u banāhā" (79:27) — the raised sky; "bunyānuhum alladhī banaw" (9:110) the structure they built. The building nouns match: bunyān raised "min al-qawā'id" from the foundations (16:26), "asasa bunyānahu 'alā taqwā" founded his structure upon (9:109), "al-samā' binā'an" the sky as a raised canopy (2:22; 40:64), bannā' the builder (38:37), ghuraf mabniyya built chambers (39:20), bunyān marṣūṣ a compacted structure (61:4). In every case: an entity raised so as to stand, resting on / issuing from a base. (2) KINSHIP. The 173 nominal occurrences overwhelmingly denote offspring/descendants: ibn Maryam, banū Isrā'īl, banū Ādam, abnā'akum, banāt, banūn/banīn ("al-mālu wa-l-banūn" 18:46). Subtracting form and construction, the residue is the same shape: the child is the constituted issue that stands as the continuation of its progenitor-source. This is confirmed INTERNALLY by two pivot usages: "ibn al-sabīl" (2:177; 9:60; 17:26; 8:41…) — the traveler, literally "offspring of the road," where no biological birth is involved and the term can only mean "one constitutively derived-from / belonging-to X"; and the group term "banū Isrā'īl / banū Ādam," a whole lineage raised up from a single named source. These show that "ibn/banū" encodes "constituted-issue-of-a-source," exactly the abstraction the building family instantiates physically. Even the polemical cases fit: "naḥnu abnā'u llāh" (5:18), "'Uzayr ibn Allāh / al-Masīḥ ibn Allāh" (9:30) assert precisely a source-constitution relation, and "mā ja'ala ad'iyā'akum abnā'akum" (33:4) denies that adoption creates the genuine built-from-you relation — the residue is the very thing being affirmed or denied.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: Verb I banā = the ACT of constituting/raising; verbal nouns bunyān/binā' = the built PRODUCT; participle bannā' = the AGENT; passive mabniyy = the product-as-affected; the relational nouns ibn/bint/banū/banāt/abnā' = the constituted ISSUE. Form fixes act vs. product vs. agent vs. issue, not the core. CONSTRUCTION: 'alā ("build upon" 9:109; 18:21) supplies the base/footing vector; li- ("build for" 37:97; 40:36; 66:11) supplies a beneficiary; the iḍāfa "ibn X" (Maryam, al-sabīl, Isrā'īl, Ādam, Allāh) supplies WHICH source — the construction names the source and vector but does not create the constitution relation. PARTICIPANTS (God raising the sky, Pharaoh a tower, parents their sons, Jinn as builders) and CONTEXT (eschatological "māl wa banūn," inheritance/marriage law in 4:11/4:23, Israelite narrative, Christological polemic) are all subtractable. Residue after subtraction, present in all 184: a raised/derived standing-entity constituted from a source-base.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The single hardest case is the pure construction cluster, e.g. "wa-l-samā'a banaynāhā bi-aydin" (51:47:2:1) and "ibni lī ṣarḥan" (40:36:4:1), set against the ~160 pure-kinship occurrences: the two evoke visibly different images (masonry vs. begetting), which threatens to split the root into two homonyms rather than one residue. It reconciles because the internal data itself supplies the bridge: "ibn al-sabīl" (e.g. 2:177:27:2) proves "ibn" is NOT restricted to biological birth but means "constitutively derived-from / belonging-to X," and "banū Isrā'īl / banū Ādam" name whole lineages raised from one source — so the kinship family already trades in the abstract "constituted-issue-from-a-base" that the building family renders physically. The shared residue (derived standing-entity + source-relation) is genuinely recoverable in the construction cases (a structure raised upon its qawā'id) and the kinship cases (a descendant raised from a progenitor) alike; nothing contradicts it. The reconciliation is real but requires an abstraction step, which is why the strength is capped at MODERATE.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is a two-headed (near-homonymous) account: core-A "to build/erect a structure" (verbs + bunyān/binā'/bannā'/mabniyy, ~20 occ.) and core-B "offspring/descendant" (ibn/banū/banāt/abnā', ~160 occ.), treated as distinct meanings rather than one residue. This also "covers" the data descriptively. Internal evidence partly arbitrates AGAINST full split and FOR unity: ibn al-sabīl (derived belonging, non-biological) and banū Isrā'īl (a lineage raised from a source) show the kinship terms are not simply "child" but "constituted-issue-of," which is the same abstraction the building family instantiates — a single center is therefore more economical than two homonyms. What the internal evidence CANNOT settle is the DIRECTION/priority of that center (is "beget" a metaphor of "build," or vice versa?): frequency cannot decide this (and majority is disallowed), and no occurrence stages the two senses together to fix priority. The conceptual center is thus unified but directionally underdetermined — hence MODERATE, not STRONG.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest kinship neighbor is wld (w-l-d, walad/wālid/mawlūd): wld foregrounds the biological birthing/parturition event and the immediate generative bond, whereas bny foregrounds the child as a constituted STANDING extension of a source — which is why bny yields the lineage/group term banū (banū Isrā'īl, banū Ādam) and the non-biological ibn al-sabīl, contexts where wld would not fit. Related is dhurriyya/nsl (progeny as scattered seed), which foregrounds proliferation, versus bny's singular constituted unit resting on its source. Nearest building neighbors are '-m-r (to develop/populate/maintain a place) and sh-y-d/ṣ-r-ḥ (masonry/erection): '-m-r foregrounds inhabiting and keeping a place flourishing, while bny foregrounds the raising of the structure itself upon a foundation. Falsifiability: the unity is refuted if the corpus shows bny used for the sheer act of parturition/birthing with no standing-entity sense, or for merely populating/maintaining an already-built place, or wld/'-m-r used for erecting a structure from its foundations — none of which occur in these 184.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — a constituted, raised-up standing-entity issuing from and resting upon a source-base — is recoverable in every one of the 184 occurrences, with zero contradictions. The building family exhibits it physically (structures raised min al-qawā'id / 'alā a footing: 16:26, 9:109, 18:21, 40:36, 51:47, 78:12), and the kinship family exhibits it generatively (descendants and the lineage/relational terms). Crucially the bridge is INTERNALLY attested, not imported: ibn al-sabīl and banū Isrā'īl/Ādam show that ibn/banū encode "constituted-issue-of-a-source" rather than mere biological child, matching the building abstraction; and the polemical/legal cases (5:18; 9:30; 33:4) turn precisely on affirming or denying that source-constitution relation, so the residue is present even where the relation is contested. Strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG because unifying the physically-built structure with the begotten child requires a genuine abstraction/metaphorical-extension step, and internal evidence, while favoring one center over two homonyms, cannot fix the direction of that center (build-first vs. beget-first) — the conceptual core is robust but underdetermined. No occurrence stays unreconciled, so inconsistent_refs is empty and clean presence is claimed honestly at the abstract level.

adversarial_verification.notes: Read all 184 occurrences. The candidate covers the two overt families robustly: (1) BUILDING — all 11 verbal forms (18:21, 26:128, 37:97, 40:36, 50:6, 51:47, 66:11, 78:12, 79:27, 91:5, 9:110) plus bunyan/bina'/banna'/mabniyya nouns (16:26, 9:109 x2, 9:110, 2:22, 40:64, 38:37, 39:20, 61:4, 18:21, 37:97) are all literally erected standing structures resting on a base; no failure. (2) KINSHIP — banu Isra'il/Adam (lineage from a named source), ibn Maryam, banat, abna', banun, ibnata Imran (66:12), ibnatayya (28:27), ibn umma (7:150; 20:94) all read as constituted issue / standing continuation of a progenitor. Polemical cases (5:18 abna'u llah; 9:30 ibn Allah x2; 33:4 ad'iya'akum abna'akum; God's daughters 16:57/37:149/43:16/52:39/6:100) assert or deny a source-constitution relation, so they support the residue rather than break it. HARDEST CASES: the ibn al-sabil idiom (the 8 listed word_refs, all 'wayfarer/son of the road'). The discovery leans on these as internal proof, but adversarially they are the candidate's weakest link: the traveler is not constituted-by, built-up-from, or a standing continuation OF the road — no progenitor, no birth, no construction. The candidate can only retain them by quietly demoting its load-bearing component ('RAISED-UP/built-up product') to a generic relational 'belonging-to X'. That is a genuine over-breadth dilution: the distinctive half of the invariant is ABSENT there, and only the weak source/association half survives. This does not amount to full refutation because the building<->kinship bridge is coherent and classically attested (offspring = what is 'built' from the father), and it discriminates against nearest neighbors: wld (begetting/birth) never carries the construction sense, and 'ss/asasa ('found') stands beside bunyan in 9:109 as the distinct founding act, while the group-lineage banu-X is a bny specialty. So distinctiveness holds at root level and the failure condition is clear (falsifiable), but the idiomatic relational uses prove the 'constituted/raised' residue is not strictly invariant. Hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, with the ibn al-sabil cluster flagged as the over-breadth problem set.
